title: Fairness Definitions in Language Models Explained

bias_targets.methodology: Assessed across intrinsic and extrinsic metrics, including word embedding associations (WEAT/SEAT), masked token probability differences, counterfactual prompt substitution in text generation, attention head-based disparities, and true positive rate gaps in occupation classification.

Evaluated using word embedding associations, pseudo-log-likelihood on stereotypical sentences (StereoSet), context-based disparity in question answering (BBQ), and inference bias scores in cross-lingual natural language inference tasks.

Measured through word embedding similarity tests, stereotypical association probabilities in question answering (Natural Questions), and counterfactual token fairness in clinical datasets (Heart Disease).
Assessed via masked token prediction probabilities (XNLI), pseudo-log-likelihood metrics, and demographic representation disparity in ambiguous question answering contexts (BBQ).
Evaluated using pseudo-log-likelihood metrics on stereotypical sentence pairs (CrowS-Pairs) and performance disparity metrics in question answering tasks (Natural Questions).
Measured through intrinsic similarity-based disparities (WEAT, SEAT, CEAT) by comparing embedding associations between mental/physical illness terms and temporary/permanent attributes.
Assessed using demographic representation metrics to measure the frequency and normalized probability of mentions in text generated by language models (CrowS-Pairs).

Evaluated using Normalized Position Disparity (NPD) to measure how encoder-decoder models disproportionately emphasize specific token positions (e.g., early text) of a source text during summarization.

Assessed via algorithmic disparity metrics such as Lexical Frequency Profile (LFP) and Morphological Complexity Disparity (MCD) to measure model bias toward high-frequency words or dominant morphological forms.
